text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav army delegation headed by chief of general staff General Momcilo Perisic made a one-day visit to Austria's army, discussing army cooperation.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic is visiting Austria.
- Croatian customs guards will take up position on the Croatian-Yugoslav border in eastern Slavonia from November 1. Yugoslavs required to have valid Croatian visas when visiting the region.

- Yugoslavia's biggest hydroelectric power plant Djerdap I completed its annual production plan of five billion kw/hrs of electricity and will produce an extra one billion kw/hrs by the end of the year.
- Komercijalna banka and Beobanka from Thursday started selling American Express travellers cheques.

- Yugoslavia to launch initiative for an atomic-free Danube, banning construction of atomic power plants and transport of nuclear material and waste on the river, says Serbian ecology minister Jordan Aleksic.
- Director of Zastava Arms Branko Smigic warns workers about illegal interruption of work in response to their resumed protests after a 19-day break.
- Perpetrator of the kidnapping and killing of 21 Yugoslav citizens in the Strpci train station found after almost four years.
NASA BORBA

- Bosnian Serb army commander General Ratko Mladic and other top Bosnian Serb officers have not yet been retired by Bosnian President Biljana Plavsic but this will happen very soon, a source in Pale said.
- The import of some 100,000 tonnes of sugar has dragged down domestic sugar prices and threatens to result in the closure of half of the 15 sugar factories.
- Citroen-Jucit opened in Yugoslavia, planning to cover car imports with exports of products from Yugoslav factories, says director Marko Laketa.
- Montenegro buys two Fokker-28 planes in Brussels for Montenegro airlines.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Five Yugoslav ships will remain blocked in U.S. ports until process of succession of the former federation is completed.
- Yugoslavs have difficulties in getting Greek visas - three to five days of waiting needed. Instead of issuing 2,000 to 3,000 visas a day the Greeek embassy now issues 200 at the most.
BORBA
- Delegation of Slovak iron and steel works Kosice says the works, together with Slovak banks, are ready to participate in the realisation of a number of projects in Yugoslavia.
--Belgrade Newsroom 381 11 222 4254
